description: Each trader type's size is the number of transaction records belonging to traders of that type.

a.request: Match each transaction record to its trader (`trdref` = `tradereg`, exact text match) and drop records with no matching trader. Then, for each trader type (`tradekind`), count the transaction records. Count every record, so a trader with five records adds five. Traders with no type form their own group. Which trader types have a count strictly above the plain average of the per-type counts? For each one, show the trader type, its count, that count divided by the total of all the per-type counts, and the count minus the average. Don't round anything, and return nothing if the average is missing.
a.sql:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT tr.tradekind, COUNT(*) AS transaction_count
  FROM transactionrecord AS r
  JOIN trader AS tr ON r.trdref = tr.tradereg
  GROUP BY tr.tradekind
), summary AS (
  SELECT tradekind,
         transaction_count,
         SUM(transaction_count) OVER () AS total_count,
         AVG(transaction_count) OVER () AS average_count
  FROM counts
)
SELECT tradekind,
       transaction_count,
       transaction_count::numeric / total_count AS proportion_of_total,
       transaction_count - average_count AS difference_from_average
FROM summary
WHERE transaction_count > average_count;

c.request: Using the transaction records matched to their traders (`trdref` = `tradereg`, exact text match, dropping records with no matching trader), how big is each trader type (`tradekind`) in this data? Traders with no type form their own group. Which trader types have a count strictly above the plain average of the per-type counts? For each one, show the trader type, its count, that count divided by the total of all the per-type counts, and the count minus the average. Don't round anything, and return nothing if the average is missing. Each trader type's size is the number of transaction records belonging to traders of that type.
c.sql:
WITH per_type AS (
  SELECT tr.tradekind, COUNT(*) AS transaction_count
  FROM transactionrecord AS trr
  JOIN trader AS tr ON trr.trdref = tr.tradereg
  GROUP BY tr.tradekind
), stats AS (
  SELECT tradekind, transaction_count,
         SUM(transaction_count) OVER () AS total_count,
         AVG(transaction_count) OVER () AS average_count
  FROM per_type
)
SELECT tradekind, transaction_count,
       transaction_count::numeric / NULLIF(total_count, 0) AS proportion_of_total,
       transaction_count - average_count AS count_minus_average
FROM stats
WHERE average_count IS NOT NULL
  AND transaction_count > average_count;

b.request: Count transaction records matched to a trader by exact `transactionrecord.trdref = trader.tradereg`, excluding records with no matching trader, and group them by `trader.tradekind`, treating NULL types as one group. Compute the plain average of these per-type counts, and return only types whose count is strictly above that average, showing the type, count, count divided by the sum of all per-type counts, and count minus the average without rounding; return no rows if the average is missing
b.sql:
WITH type_counts AS (
  SELECT t.tradekind, COUNT(*) AS record_count
  FROM transactionrecord AS tr
  JOIN trader AS t ON tr.trdref = t.tradereg
  GROUP BY t.tradekind
), stats AS (
  SELECT AVG(record_count) AS avg_count, SUM(record_count) AS total_count
  FROM type_counts
)
SELECT tc.tradekind, tc.record_count,
       tc.record_count::numeric / s.total_count AS count_share,
       tc.record_count - s.avg_count AS above_average
FROM type_counts AS tc
CROSS JOIN stats AS s
WHERE tc.record_count > s.avg_count;

d.request: For each trader type, count the transaction records belonging to traders of that type. Treat traders with no type as their own group. Which types have counts strictly above the plain average of the per-type counts? Show each qualifying type, its count, that count divided by the total of all per-type counts, and the count minus the average. Don’t round anything, and return nothing if the average is missing.
d.sql:
WITH type_counts AS (
  SELECT t.tradekind, COUNT(tr.transreg) AS transaction_count
  FROM trader AS t
  LEFT JOIN transactionrecord AS tr
    ON tr.trdref = t.tradereg
  GROUP BY t.tradekind
), stats AS (
  SELECT
    AVG(transaction_count) AS avg_count,
    SUM(transaction_count) AS total_count
  FROM type_counts
)
SELECT
  tc.tradekind,
  tc.transaction_count,
  tc.transaction_count::numeric / NULLIF(s.total_count, 0) AS share_of_total,
  tc.transaction_count - s.avg_count AS above_average
FROM type_counts AS tc
CROSS JOIN stats AS s
WHERE s.avg_count IS NOT NULL
  AND tc.transaction_count > s.avg_count;
